title: Health and the Body
description: Build essential vocabulary for talking about body parts, describing common illnesses and symptoms, and communicating at the doctor's. Ideal for A1 completers who want to handle health situations confidently in English.

content.content: {"time":1700000201000,"blocks":[{"id":"aB1cD2eF3g","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Let's learn the parts of the head and face:"}},{"id":"hI4jK5lM6n","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["head — the top part of your body","forehead — the part above your eyes","eye — what you see with (plural: eyes)","ear — what you hear with (plural: ears)","nose — what you smell and breathe with","mouth — what you eat and speak with","tooth — hard white thing in your mouth (plural: teeth)","chin — the bottom of your face","cheek — the side of your face","neck — connects your head to your body"]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: My forehead, cheeks, chin, and neck are all parts of your head and face.

questions.text: You use your ___ to hear sounds.

content.content: {"time":1700000202000,"blocks":[{"id":"oP7qR8sT9u","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Now let's learn the rest of the body:"}},{"id":"vW0xY1zA2b","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["shoulder — connects your arm to your body","arm — from shoulder to hand","elbow — the joint in the middle of your arm","wrist — connects your hand to your arm","hand — at the end of your arm","finger — you have 5 on each hand","chest — the front of your body above the stomach","back — the rear side of your body","stomach — where food goes when you eat","knee — the joint in the middle of your leg","ankle — connects your foot to your leg","foot — at the end of your leg (plural: feet)"]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: I hurt my knee when I fell. She broke her wrist playing tennis.
I hurt my [knee] when I fell down the stairs. The doctor looked at my [back] and said I needed to rest. She broke her [wrist] playing tennis. He has a pain in his [chest].

{"time":1700000203000,"blocks":[{"id":"cD3eF4gH5i","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Here are common illnesses and how to talk about them:"}},{"id":"jK6lM7nO8p","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["a cold — a common illness with a runny nose and sore throat","the flu / influenza — a more serious illness, like a bad cold with fever","a fever — a high body temperature (above 38°C)","a cough — you make a loud sound from your throat","a sore throat — your throat hurts when you swallow","a runny nose — liquid coming out of your nose"]}},{"id":"qR9sT0uV1w","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Grammar — 'have' for illnesses:
I have a cold. / She has the flu. / He had a fever last night."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

{"time":1700000204000,"blocks":[{"id":"xY2zA3bC4d","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"We describe pain with the word ache or pain. Common expressions:"}},{"id":"eF5gH6iJ7k","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["headache — pain in your head","stomachache / stomach ache — pain in your stomach","backache / back pain — pain in your back","toothache — pain in your tooth","earache — pain in your ear"]}},{"id":"lM8nO9pQ0r","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"We also use: My [body part] hurts / aches
My back hurts. / My head aches. / My knee is painful."}},{"id":"sT1uV2wX3y","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Past simple: My stomach hurt all night. / I had a terrible headache yesterday."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: I have a terrible headache. My back hurts and I have a stomachache.

{"time":1700000205000,"blocks":[{"id":"zA4bC5dE6f","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Sometimes we injure ourselves in accidents. Learn this vocabulary:"}},{"id":"gH7iJ8kL9m","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["cut — a sharp wound on the skin","bruise — a dark mark on the skin after a hit","sprain — a stretched or torn muscle around a joint (e.g. sprained ankle)","fracture / broken bone — a bone is cracked or broken","burn — skin damaged by heat or fire","bleed — blood comes out of a wound"]}},{"id":"nO0pQ1rS2t","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Past simple of injury verbs:
cut → cut (same!), break → broke, sprain → sprained, burn → burned/burnt"}},{"id":"uV3wX4yZ5a","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Example: She fell and broke her ankle. / He cut his finger while cooking."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.content: {"time":1700000206000,"blocks":[{"id":"bC6dE7fG8h","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"When you visit a doctor, you need to describe how you feel. Use these structures:"}},{"id":"iJ9kL0mN1o","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Describing symptoms:"}},{"id":"pQ2rS3tU4v","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["I feel... → I feel dizzy / sick / tired / weak.","I have... → I have a fever / a cough / a rash.","My [body part] hurts / aches. → My chest hurts.","I can't... → I can't sleep / breathe well / walk properly."]}},{"id":"wX5yZ6aB7c","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Useful adjectives:"}},{"id":"dE8fG9hI0j","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["dizzy — the room seems to be spinning","nauseous — feeling like you want to vomit","exhausted — extremely tired","swollen — bigger than normal (swollen ankle)"]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.instructions: Practise telling the doctor your symptoms
content.targetPhrase: I feel dizzy and nauseous. My chest hurts and I can't breathe well.

content.text: I feel dizzy and nauseous. My knee is swollen and I can't walk properly.

content.content:
{"time":1700000207000,"blocks":[{"id":"kL1mN2oP3q","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Read this typical dialogue at the doctor's:"}},{"id":"rS4tU5vW6x","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Doctor: Good morning. What seems to be the problem?
Patient: I don't feel well. I have a terrible headache and a sore throat.
Doctor: How long have you had these symptoms?
Patient: Since yesterday morning. I also have a fever — 38.5 degrees.
Doctor: Let me examine you. Open your mouth, please. Yes, your throat looks red and inflamed.
Patient: Is it serious?
Doctor: No, it's a throat infection. I'll prescribe some antibiotics. Take them three times a day with food.
Patient: Thank you, doctor. How long will it take to get better?
Doctor: You should feel better in 3–4 days. Get plenty of rest and drink a lot of water."}},{"id":"yZ7aB8cD9e","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Key vocabulary from the dialogue: symptoms, inflamed, prescribe, antibiotics, get better."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.instructions: Practise the patient's opening line at the doctor's
content.targetPhrase: I don't feel well. I have a terrible headache and a sore throat.

content.text: What seems to be the problem? How long have you had these symptoms?
Doctor: What seems to be the [problem]? Patient: I have a sore [throat] and a [fever]. Doctor: How long have you had these [symptoms]? I'll [prescribe] you some medicine.

content.content: {"time":1700000208000,"blocks":[{"id":"fG0hI1jK2l","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"We use should / shouldn't to give health advice:"}},{"id":"mN3oP4qR5s","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["You should drink more water. (это хорошая идея)","You shouldn't eat junk food. (это плохая идея)","You should get more sleep.","You shouldn't drink too much coffee."]}},{"id":"tU6vW7xY8z","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"We also use had better for stronger advice:"}},{"id":"aB9cD0eF1g","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["You had better see a doctor.
